raw_response:
I’m just farming 3.5 mu of spring maize, so I won’t do anything fancy this year. My land is small, and with some people working off-farm, I have to keep things steady and not spend too much cash at once. What I usually look at is what worked on my field before and what other people nearby are doing. If the weather is normal, I’ll plant after the soil warms up, use the hybrid seed the local dealer has, put most fertilizer at planting, and then see how the crop looks before adding more. I have well water, so if it turns dry, I can irrigate, but pumping costs money, so I won’t water unless the maize really needs it. For pests and weeds, I usually don’t spray unless I see a problem, but weeds in maize can get bad, so I’ll likely use herbicide once to save labor.
